fatal_errors: The proposed alloy, AlCoCrFeNi2.1, does not match the composition-constrained Al0.7CoCrFeNi target.
The intervention adds severe plastic deformation and uses 10–20 GPa rather than reconstructing the direct hexahedron-anvil HPHT treatment at 6 GPa and 1473 K for 2 hours.
The proposed 600–900 °C temperature window excludes the target treatment temperature of approximately 1200 °C.
The HIP comparison is confounded because the extreme-pressure group also receives severe plastic deformation, so it cannot isolate pressure as the causal variable.
explanation: The hypothesis captures the broad problem—an FCC/B2 lamellar eutectic alloy, interfacial cracking, high-pressure processing, patterned microstructure, and a conventional-HIP control—but misses most target-specific details. It predicts globularization or reticulation rather than a hierarchical pattern with coherent interfaces, and its mechanism emphasizes lamellar breakup and speculative pressure-induced stacking-fault-energy changes rather than preferential dislocation transfer, converging phase-resolved GND densities, and activation of stacking faults, microbands, and twins. The predicted mechanical outcome is also substantially weaker and less specific than the demonstrated approximately 1150 MPa strength and 36% uniform elongation. The cited evidence establishes dual-phase behavior and pressure effects in other alloy systems, but it does not directly support the proposed 10–20 GPa SPD-plus-annealing route in this composition. The experiment has explicit falsification criteria and useful microscopy and tensile measurements, but requires matched SPD-plus-annealing controls at conventional and extreme pressure to isolate the pressure effect.
